Attaching a short spreadsheet with the specific questions our privacy team tracks (see: Acme_Telemetry_Questions.xlsx) — feel free to drop answers inline.

Subject: Re: Follow up on demo — telemetry & cookie details (technical)

Hi Jamie — quick technical clarifications following Logan’s note: 

Console telemetry (what we collect):
- Event categories: API call metadata (model id, token counts, latency), UI events (route, feature flags used), anonymized error stacks.
- PII handling: prompt text is not forwarded to third-party analytics. Where we need payload-level traces for debugging, they are stored in a separate secure trace store with restricted access and short retention (default 30 days) and are redacted automatically.
- IP handling: source IPs are truncated/masked for analytics aggregation; full IPs are only available in audit logs for customers with Dedicated/Private where required.
- Cookies: console uses a single strictly-necessary session cookie and an opt-in analytics cookie (category: analytics). The docs site uses a static analytics pixel; cookies there are limited to analytics and expire after 90 days.
- Opt-out / controls: Customers can disable telemetry collection for their account (console toggle) or request a data collection opt-out in the Dedicated/Private deployment.

Retention & export:
- Default telemetry metric retention: 90 days aggregated; raw traces 30 days.
- Audit logs for Dedicated: 1 year by default (configurable).

If useful, I can export the console cookie mapping and sample telemetry schemas ahead of the call.

— Marcus
Product Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

Attachment: console_cookie_mapping_v2.csv (updated mapping available on request)

Priya / Jamie — great questions. Answers and logistics below: 

1) Prompts in traces: support/debug traces may include original prompts only when a customer provides explicit consent or when a privileged debug session is opened; access is gated via RBAC and recorded in audit logs. By default, we store only redacted/hashed prompt content in telemetry. We can arrange a contractual clause to restrict support access if required.

2) Docs analytics vendor: the docs site uses an internally-hosted analytics pipeline (no third-party marketing cookies). We do not place marketing or ad-tracking cookies on the docs domain.

3) DPA: we can accept your DPA and SCCs in most cases; Vanessa will follow up with details and our legal contact.

Next steps / proposed timeline: 
- Today: We’ll upload the prefilled questionnaire to your portal (Marcus/Logan).
- Tue, May 11: 30m security sync with Redwood infra/security engineer (please propose time slots; we prefer morning PST).
- Wed, May 12: Vanessa to surface DPA redline, SOC2 attestation and HIPAA checklist.

If that timeline works, I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue and upload the content to your portal this afternoon.
